title: Reference-dependent learning explained reward choices in humans and rats
summary: Choice behavior in three experiments with 72 human participants and 44 rats showed preferences for contextually high-value options despite objective cost. A reference-point-dependent learning model fit observed choices and reproduced transfer-phase choice patterns better than the absolute-value account. Differences between human and rat task designs limit direct comparison of some model parameters; fitted models do not establish a neural mechanism.
